Name: 12_markdown_img_html_pdf
Representative_Docs: ['Related to the base image abstraction leaking. ---- We could add all the post-processing config directly in this parser since this parser is responsible for assembling the final documents at the end of the day. What do you think if we make this? It's simple to think about / simple to document and people will discover this as part of the interface ``` format_images: Optional[Literal["html-img", "markdown-img"]] = None, ``` ', "This is will be pretty confusing for users and also has incorrect behavior -- I doubt a chat model will understand what `html-img` means for a format. I think it's evidence that the base abstraction of BaseImageBlobParser is leaking, the code that wraps things into html-img or markdown-img should just be in the caller.", "Users will not understand what this means from looking at the API reference docs. Could we improve until this is self-explanation from just looking at the API Reference? Perhaps a type update to: `Optional[Literal['markdown-link', 'html-img']]` and make the literal names more specific? For example, * None = return the content as is * `markdown-link` = wrap the content into a markdown link, w/ link pointing to... * `html-img` = wrap the content as the `alt` text of an tag and link to ... Also consider a clash against a potential future implementation: The new implementation accepts a screenshot of an **entire** PDF page and create a markdown representation of it. (i.e., the output is `markdown` here, but the has a very different meaning now and we don't want to rewrap it all as a markdown link). Perhaps renaming `format` to `wrap_as` would be helpful for communicating what this does?"]
